title: How Many Big 12 Titles Did Lincoln Riley Win at Oklahoma?
question: How many Big 12 championships did Lincoln Riley win as Oklahoma's head coach?
answer: Four. Lincoln Riley won the Big 12 championship in each of his first four seasons as OU's head coach, 2017 through 2020, and led the Sooners to the College Football Playoff in 2017, 2018 and 2019.
summary: Lincoln Riley won four straight Big 12 titles at Oklahoma from 2017 to 2020 and went 55-10, the best winning percentage of any Sooner head coach.
body: Lincoln Riley's run at Oklahoma was short but packed with hardware. Bob Stoops hired him as offensive coordinator in January 2015, and when Stoops retired on June 7, 2017, the Sooners promoted Riley, then 33 and the youngest head coach in the FBS. He won the Big 12 in each of his first four seasons.

The first three teams all went 12-2 and reached the College Football Playoff, including a double-overtime Rose Bowl semifinal against Georgia after the 2017 season. The 2019 crown came the hard way: a 30-23 overtime win over Baylor in Arlington on Dec. 7, 2019. That gave OU five straight Big 12 titles counting the 2016 crown under Stoops, making it the first Power Five team since Alabama from 1971 to 1975 to win five consecutive outright league championships.

Title No. 4 for Riley arrived on Dec. 19, 2020, when Oklahoma held off Iowa State 27-21, sealed by a late Tre Brown interception. The Associated Press noted it was OU's sixth straight outright Big 12 title, the longest Power Five streak since the Sooners' own run of 12 straight Big Eight titles from 1948 to 1959.

Riley went 55-10 at Oklahoma, an .846 winning percentage that is the best of any full-time Sooner head coach. He coached back-to-back Heisman winners in Baker Mayfield and Kyler Murray before leaving to become USC's head coach on Nov. 28, 2021.
